quarterly_data.quarter: SUMCO press release: ANNUAL REPORT 2025 (Jan. 1, 2025 to (06-26-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Annual report (company claim): SUMCO holds a worldwide share of over 50% in wafers for leading-edge logic chips and supplies wafers for leading-edge memory, including stacked-structure memory. The company says it supplies products preferentially to customers who concluded longer-term sales contracts with economically rational pricing.
quarterly_data.figure: over 50% share in leading-edge logic wafers (company claim)

quarterly_data.quarter: SUMCO press release: ANNUAL REPORT 2025 (Jan. 1, 2025 to (06-26-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Annual report (risk section): SUMCO has long-term purchasing agreements for polycrystalline silicon with the world's major polysilicon makers, but because demand forecasts at signing diverged from the consumption outlook, it is currently holding excess inventories, which may limit opportunities to reduce raw-material costs until inventories return to a proper level.

quarterly_data.quarter: SUMCO press release: ANNUAL REPORT 2025 (Jan. 1, 2025 to (06-26-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Annual report: the new leading-edge 300mm wafer factory (greenfield decided in 2021) is being phased into operation in the Imari district and existing plants are to be upgraded; President Jiro Ryuta says investment timing for the Yoshinogari land, acquired for future demand growth, will be decided by carefully monitoring market trends. FY2025 capex fell to 79.9 billion yen as greenfield investments were largely completed; CFO: depreciation (115.6 billion yen in FY2025) is expected to peak in fiscal year 2026 and decline in fiscal year 2027 and beyond, leading to a recovery in earnings. Outlook: 200mm demand expected to remain at the current level despite AI data center-related growth; 150mm and smaller projected to contract in the long term.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 capex 79.9 billion yen; depreciation 115.6 billion yen, peak expected in FY2026
